chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) who said:
The pillars of disbelief are four: desire, fear, discontent, and anger.

key_terms.أركان: Pillars, foundational supports — the essential components without which something cannot stand
key_terms.الرغبة: Desire, worldly craving — excessive attachment to material gain
key_terms.الرهبة: Fear, dread — cowardly fear that prevents one from upholding truth
key_terms.السخط: Discontent, displeasure — being dissatisfied with divine decree
key_terms.الغضب: Anger, wrath — uncontrolled rage that overwhelms reason
key_terms.الكفر: Disbelief, rejection of faith — denial of God and His guidance

ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars of disbelief according to Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identified four emotional dispositions that form the foundations of disbelief (kufr): desire (raghba), which drives one to pursue worldly gains at the expense of faith; fear (rahba), which leads to cowardice in upholding truth; discontent (sakhat), which breeds ingratitude toward divine decree; and anger (ghadab), which clouds sound judgment. This teaching was delivered to the community as a warning about the psychological roots that undermine faith.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from la-Husayn . Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma`il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as) from the Messenger of Allah (s). He said:
The pillars of disbelief are four: (1) desire, (2) fear, (3) discontent, and (4) anger.
